Short term and long term reasons Short term O’Neill did not receive the support that he had hoped for in the so called crossroads election that took place on 24 th February 1969. There was little or no evidence of the hoped for support from Catholic voters and there was a reduction in unionist support. His party was divided and O’Neill had only managed to hold on to his own Bannside seat by 1,400 votes as the Reverend Ian Paisley stood against him and won a considerable amount of support. This put great pressure on O’Neill to step down. He struggled on for two more months but resigned on 28 th April 1969. During the months prior to the election O’Neill seemed to be losing control of the situation.
